parallelParkingDescription: Parallel parking means parking your car parallel to the curb, between two parked vehicles. It's an essential driving skill, especially in cities and during driving tests.
chooseSpot: Choose a spot that's at least 1.5 times your car's length
indicatorSlow: Turn on your indicator and approach slowly
pullUpParallel: Pull up parallel to the car in front of the space
leaveTwoFeet: Leave about 2 feet (half a meter) between the cars
rearBumpersAligned: Make sure your rear bumpers are aligned
reverseGear: Put the car in reverse gear
steeringWheelCurb: Turn the steering wheel fully toward the curb (right, in most countries)
reverseSlowly: Begin reversing slowly into the space
frontBumperClears: When your front bumper clears the rear bumper of the front car, turn the wheel in the opposite direction (left)
continueStraightening: Continue reversing while straightening the wheels
moveForwardBackward: Move forward/backward slightly to center your vehicle
inchesFromCurb: Make sure you're 6–12 inches from the curb and parallel
tooFarAlignment: Being too far from the front car during alignment
wrongSteeringTime: Not turning the steering at the right time
hittingCurb: Hitting the curb or bumping another car
forgettingMirrors: Forgetting to use mirrors and blind spot checks
reverseParkingDescription: Also known as Back-in Parking, this technique involves reversing into a parking space rather than driving in forward. It gives better visibility when exiting the spot and is often safer in busy parking lots.
makeSureSpotWide: Make sure the spot is wide enough for your vehicle
indicatorParkingSpot: Turn on your indicator toward the parking spot
driveForwardSlightlyAhead: Drive forward so your car is slightly ahead of the space
leaveThreeFourFeet: Leave about 3–4 feet (1 meter) between your car and the parked vehicles
alignRearBumper: Align your car so your rear bumper lines up with the front of the space
lookSideMirrors: Look in side mirrors, rearview mirror, and over your shoulder
ensureAreaClear: Ensure the area behind you is clear of people or obstacles
turnSteeringWheelDirection: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the space
moveSlowlyAdjust: Move slowly and adjust as needed
useReferencePoints: Use reference points (like lines or parked cars) to stay centered
straightenWheels: Once the back of your car is mostly in, begin to straighten the wheels
reverseUntilFully: Reverse until your car is fully within the lines
ensureVehicleCentered: Ensure the vehicle is centered, straight, and not too close to any car
applyHandbrakeGear: Apply handbrake and put the gear in park (P)
roundaboutDrivingDescription: Roundabouts are circular intersections designed to improve traffic flow and reduce accidents. Understanding how to use them correctly is essential for safe driving.
howToDriveRoundabout: How to Drive Through a Roundabout
slowDownNear: Slow down as you near the roundabout
lookSignsLane: Look for signs and lane markings to choose the correct lane (especially at multi-lane roundabouts)
useIndicatorsTurning: Use your indicators if you're turning left or right
giveWayTraffic: Give way to traffic already in the roundabout coming from your right side
stopIfNeeded: Stop if needed and only enter when it's safe and clear
doNotChangeLanes: Do not change lanes once inside
signalLeftPassing: Signal left after passing the exit just before yours
exitCarefullyChecking: Exit carefully, checking for pedestrians or cyclists

mainHeading: How to Properly Adjust Car Mirrors
step1: 🚘 Step 1: Sit in Your Normal Driving Position
step1Point1: Sit up straight and adjust your seat first
step1Point2: Make sure you're in your usual posture with hands on the wheel
step2: 🔄 Step 2: Adjust the Rearview Mirror (Inside Mirror)
step2Point1: Aim it to see as much of the rear window as possible
step2Point2: You should not move your head to see directly behind you
step3: 📐 Step 3: Adjust the Left Side Mirror (Driver's Side)
step3Point1: Lean your head toward the driver's window
step3Point2: Adjust so you just barely see the edge of your car on the right side of the mirror
step3Point3: The rest should show the left lane
step4: 📐 Step 4: Adjust the Right Side Mirror (Passenger Side)
step4Point1: Lean your head toward the center of the car
step4Point2: Adjust so you can barely see the side of your car on the left side of the mirror
step4Point3: The rest should show the right lane or blind spot
benefit3: Improve rear visibility without turning your head

reverseLParking.subTitle: L Parking (Reverse into an L-Shaped Parking Space)
reverseLParking.description: L Parking is a maneuver where the driver reverses the car into a 90-degree (L-shaped) parking space, often used in driving tests and tight parking areas.

step1.title: 1. Start Position
step1.point1: Align your car parallel to the parking line, about 3 feet (1 meter) away from the entry point
step1.point2: Make sure your rear bumper is in line with the start of the parking space

step2.title: 2. Check Your Surroundings
step2.point1: Use mirrors and look over your shoulder
step2.point2: Make sure the space is clear

step4.title: 4. Turn Steering Wheel Fully Left
step4.point1: As your rear wheels cross the corner, turn the steering wheel fully to the left
step4.point2: The car will begin to rotate into the parking space

step5.title: 5. Straighten the Wheel
step5.point1: Once the car is aligned between the lines, straighten the steering wheel
step5.point2: Continue reversing straight into the space

step6.title: 6. Stop & Adjust if Needed
step6.point1: Make small adjustments to center the car if it's too close to one side
step6.point2: Ensure you're fully inside the lines

tips.title: Tips for Perfect L Parking:
tips.point2: Use your side mirrors to track your position
tips.point3: Don't panic if you need to adjust — it's normal!
